Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. This petition has been filed with the following main relief:-
"i) to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned F.I.R./ Case Crime No.0049 of 2023, dated 14.04.2023, under sections-419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 IPC, Police Station- Sujauli, District: Bahraich contained in Annexure no.1 to the writ petition;.

3. Sri S.N. Tilhari, learned A.G.A. has produced before this Court instructions dated 19.05.2023 sent from Police Station Sujauli, District Bahraich, wherein almost the same facts as have been mentioned in the impugned F.I.R. have again been mentioned in a different language.

It has been stated that predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners have been alleged to have got possession of the Raja Sethi (In F.I.R. Raja Ram Sethi) And ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 22 May, 2023

land in question through three sanads on 02.04.1965 and petitioners are subsequent purchasers from such persons who had taken the sanads from the original tenure holders.

4. It has been submitted in the instructions that at the time the said alleged sanad was granted on 02.04.1965, Notification under Section 4 of the Indian Forest Act, 1947 had already been published and, therefore, no right remained either with District Authorities or in anyone else to give sanad of the land, which was proposed to be notified as Reserved Forest under the Indian Forest Act.
Therefore, if at all such sanad was given, it was given illegally.

Because of such forged sanad in favour of Hansraj and Suresh Kumar, who later on sold the property in question to six other persons, valuable land belonging to forest Reserve Katarniaghat, Range Nishangaada, have been frittered away.
Such land has several old trees standing thereon.

5. The instructions as well as the F.I.R. also talk of a Committee being constituted under the Chairmanship of the District Magistrate, Bahraich, which submitted a report on 12.05.2022 with regard to Gata no.19.

The copy of such report prepared by the Committee is said to have been enclosed with the F.I.R.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has pointed out that the petitioners have brought on record the report dated 12.05.2022, which has been made the basis of the F.I.R., as annexure-25 of the writ petition, at page-179 of the paper book.

7. This Court has gone through the report and finds that the District Magistrate on a request being made by the office of the Chief Standing Counsel by letter dated 09.05.2022 in Writ Petition No.775 (Consolidation) of 1985: State of U.P. Vs. Vimla Sabarwal and others, had conducted the enquiry into the matter by summoning the records from the Record Room at Tehsil Nanpara.

sentences.text: The record of 1356 Fasli and 1359 Fasli were not found preserved in the record room, but the record of 1336 Fasli was found preserved.

As per the said record, there were ten plots of land initially in Gram- Hariharpur, Pargana Dharmapur, and all such land was recorded as banjar, covered by water, river & road and in the khata of Sarkar Bahadur mentioning two khewatdars, namely, Sardar Karam Singh and Sarkar Bahadur Kaiseri-Hind.
The entire land in the 1336 Fasli of Gram Hariharpur Lalpur did not show the name of any private khewatdar/ kaashtkar.

After the Notification and enforcement of the U.P. Z.A. & L.R. Act with effect from 01.07.1952 i.e. from 1360 Fasli, the Rules provided that the tenure of the possession of the land should be mentioned either "before 1360 Fasli" or "after 1360 Fasli".
In the 1364 Fasli, three Kaashtkars are mentioned in whose possession has been shown with effect from 1362 Fasli.
They are Suresh Kumar s/o Hansraj, Hansraj himself and wife of Hansraj, Pratapkunwari, all residents of Lucknow.

The District Magistrate has mentioned that it is not clear as to how the land which was recorded as banjar and belonging to Sarkar Bahadur Kaiser-i-Hind in 1336 Fasli, has been recorded in the name of three Kaashtkars with effect from 1362 Fasli i.e. with effect from 1954.

Such land has also been shown as old parti land,
whereas it was recorded as banjar land in the earlier khasra.

It has also come out in the said report that Gata No.18 was carved out of old Gata Nos.6, 7, 9 & 10, which belonged to Sarkar Bahadur Kaiser-i-Hind and stood vested in the State even from before 1952.
Land vested in the State in 1360 Fasli could not have been given to Suresh Kumar and others in 1362 Fasli.

A perusal of the report further shows that none of the three Kaashtakars as aforesaid ever cultivated the land, because had they cultivated the land, their mention would have been found in the khasra of subsequent years.

It has also been stated in the said report that on 18.10.1952, the State Government published a Notification No.617 dated 11.10.1952 notifying 564 acres of land of Gram Hariharpur Lalpur under Section 4 of the Indian Forest Act.

9. It has also been mentioned in the said report that the Bandobast i.e. the consolidation records further show the number of plot no.18 being further changed to plot nos. 18A, 34A and then plot no.21D was carved out of it and in 1364 Fasli record operation, Gata no.18 Min. has been mentioned as Jungle and departmental forest.

The alleged sanads made out in favour of Suresh Kumar and Hansraj in 1965 are fraudulent sanads as they have been mentioned to have been executed in 1965 i.e. after the Notification of 1952 under Section 4 of the Indian Forest Act.
The land having vested on 15.10.1971 under Section 20 in Katarniaghat Forest Range, it could not have been sold off by Suresh Kumar s/o Hansraj.
It has also come out that no objections were filed to Section 4 Notification by them.
10. The Consolidation operations have also mentioned that plot nos.18A and 34A were further given new numbers i.e. 21A, 21S, 21C, 21D and 19A.
There are several old trees standing thereon indicating that they are forest land since a long time ago.
Such forest land could not have been sold off by the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners.

11. After having examined the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and having perused the impugned F.I.R., we are of the opinion that the impugned F.I.R. discloses cognizable offence having been committed by the petitioners.

Hence, no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the F.I.R. or for grant of any interim relief to the petitioners.

12. At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioners says that the rights of the petitioners shall be affected in the pending writ petition because of the order passed by this Court refusing to interfere in the impugned F.I.R..

13. This Court finds that initially the counsel for the petitioners had argued before this Court that the petitioners have already relinquished their claim over the plots in question and have filed an application before the Writ-Court in Writ Petition No.775 (Cons.) of 1985 and thereafter the F.I.R.
has been lodged against them.
If the petitioners have already relinquished their claim in the pending writ petition, their interest would certainly not be affected by the dismissal of this writ petition by this Court.

14. Since the impugned F.I.R. discloses cognizable offence by the petitioner, hence, no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the F.I.R. and accordingly, the present writ petition is dismissed.
